sections.body: Think of a job as 1 whole. If someone does it alone in 6 days, they do 1/6 of the job each day. That is their rate of work. Rates of people working together add up.
Example: A takes 6 days and B takes 12 days. Together they do 1/6 + 1/12 = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the job per day. So together they take 4 days.
You can work backwards. If A and B together take 6 days, and A alone takes 10 days, then B's rate is 1/6 - 1/10 = 5/30 - 3/30 = 2/30 = 1/15. So B alone takes 15 days.

If every worker works at the same rate, use worker-days. 5 workers take 6 days, so the job is 30 worker-days. With 10 workers it takes 30 ÷ 10 = 3 days. More workers means fewer days, and the product stays the same.
A tap fills a tank in 4 hours and another tap fills it in 12 hours. How long do they take together? Check by finding the fraction filled in one hour.
The key step is turning 'takes n days' into '1/n of the job per day'. Draw a bar divided into days if fractions are shaky. Problems with a leak or drain use a subtraction instead of addition.

quiz.q: A can finish a job in 10 days and B can finish it in 15 days. How long do they take working together?
hints: Turn each time into a fraction of the job done in one day.
A does 1/10 per day and B does 1/15 per day. Add the fractions.
Example: 4 days and 12 days → 1/4 + 1/12 = 1/3 per day, so 3 days. Add 1/10 and 1/15 the same way, then flip the answer.
quiz.explain: 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6 of the job per day, so the job takes 6 days.

quiz.q: A alone can do a job in 12 days. A and B together do it in 8 days. How long would B take alone?
hints: Find the rate of A and the rate of A + B together.
Together: 1/8 per day. A alone: 1/12 per day. Subtract to get B's rate.
Example: together 6 days, A alone 10 days → 1/6 - 1/10 = 1/15, so B takes 15 days. Do 1/8 - 1/12 and flip it.
quiz.explain: 1/8 - 1/12 = 3/24 - 2/24 = 1/24 per day, so B alone takes 24 days.

quiz.q: 3 workers build a wall in 12 days. How long would 4 workers take, working at the same rate?
hints: Find the total amount of work in worker-days.
3 workers × 12 days is the size of the job. Divide by the new number of workers.
Example: 5 workers × 6 days = 30 worker-days, so 10 workers take 3 days. Use the same steps.
quiz.explain: The job is 3 × 12 = 36 worker-days. With 4 workers: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 days.
